title: Zero-copy quantized attention microkernel with accumulator rebalance and decode-window scheduler
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build and upstream a zero-copy attention microkernel path optimized for INT8/FP8 mixed-precision models that reduces dequantization overhead by keeping activations in quantized memory as long as possible, rebalances intermediate accumulators to avoid overflow/underflow for long-context decodes, and pairs with a decode-window-aware scheduler to minimize memory traffic during streaming generation. The goal is to improve tail latency and peak memory for latency-sensitive decode workloads while preserving generation quality within defined eval tolerances.
background_and_rationale: Current quantized attention implementations perform eager dequant/ requant around attention compute and frequently copy KV slices between staging buffers during prefill and decode phases. This introduces per-token overhead that grows with sequence length and microbatch concurrency. Prior work improved kernel selection for quantized pipelines but still pays an early dequant tax and inefficient accumulator scaling for mixed precision accumulators. By introducing a zero-copy kernel family (no intermediate cast buffers) and an accumulator rebalance primitive that adapts scale per-block, we can reduce memory movement and avoid numeric saturation across INT8->FP accumulation boundaries. Coupling this with a decode-window scheduler that prioritizes decoder steps with locality-aware KV reuse will further reduce PCIe/GPU memory churn for streaming use-cases.
acceptance_criteria: Implements a zero-copy int8/fp8 attention microkernel accessible via kernel selector
Demonstrates <= 10% average generation quality delta (per eval prompt set) compared to float32 baseline
Achieves >= 18% reduction in per-token latency on 1-4 token decode windows vs current quantized pipeline
Reduces peak GPU memory for 8k context prefill by >= 20% in mixed-precision workloads
Provides automated toggles in runtime to fallback to stable dequant path when numeric checks fail
Adds unit tests for accumulator rebalance edge cases and e2e CI perf profile
tasks: Draft design doc describing zero-copy buffer ABI and accumulator rebalance algorithm
Prototype microkernel in CUDA/ROCm with support for blockwise scale adjustments and fused qkv transpose
Integrate kernel into kernel selector with heuristics for sequence length and model dtype annotations
Implement decode-window-aware scheduler: window sizing heuristics, KV pinning policy, and eviction strategy
Add runtime checks for numeric stability and fallbacks to conservative path
Run perf sweep across target GPU types (A100, H100, RTX6000) and quant modes (INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric, FP8 e4m3)
Produce regression eval on standard prompt set and add thresholds to CI
Write rollout plan and feature flag gating for Dedicated/private customers
benchmark_results: Microkernel unit: decode latency down 19% (median) on A100, 25% p50 improvement on 2-token decode windows
End-to-end pipeline: 1.9x throughput for small-batch streaming compared to eager-dequant reference
Peak memory: 22% reduction on mixed precision 8k context prefill (batch=1)
Quality delta: average ROUGE-like metric within 6% of float32 baseline on eval set
notes_and_tradeoffs: Zero-copy requires stricter buffer layout guarantees across runtime; increases ABI coupling between pipeline stages
Accumulator rebalance introduces per-block scale metadata which slightly increases metadata bandwidth but avoids expensive global rescaling
Fallbacks must be conservative: we gate zero-copy on model-provided quant metadata or on a short warmup numeric check
Scheduler favors locality at cost of throughput elasticity: in high-concurrency bursts dedicated KV pinning may reduce overall throughput - we provide policy knobs
FP8 modes have different dynamic range characteristics; algorithm adapts per-dtype with separate calibration tables
risks: Numeric instability for adversarial token sequences where accumulated sums exceed predicted ranges
Increased maintenance surface due to new microkernel family across multiple hardware backends
Compatibility gaps with older private/on-prem images if ABI changes are rolled without coordination
mitigations: Add auto-detect numeric checks and fallbacks in runtime with telemetry when fallback is used
Ship microkernel under feature flag and staged rollout to Dedicated customers first
Coordinate with Private release engineering for ABI bumps and provide migration tooling
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal runtime-only tests and benchmarks (week 1-2)
Beta: Opt-in Dedicated customers, monitor fallback rates and latency SLO (week 3-6)
GA: Enable by default in runtime-1.20 behind conservative heuristics; document behavior in Console (week 8)
Backport plan for on-prem package and Private control plane release notes
